Subject: Production latency spike + routing fallback in us-west-2

Monica —

We started seeing elevated p50/p95 latencies and ~3–4% 5xx for inference in us-west-2 at ~08:40 PT. Our gateway reports that traffic was shifted to us-east-1 as part of Redwood's automated routing; latency for end-users doubled. This is impacting our chat product and we've received multiple support tickets.

Attaching a small log bundle. Can someone confirm whether this was a regional eviction, autoscaler, or something in the routing layer? We need immediate ETA and any mitigation we can apply from our side.

Thanks,
Evan

Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency spike + routing fallback in us-west-2

Short status — triage notes below:

Timeline (prelim):
- 08:38 PT: telemetry shows a short-lived spike in token queueing across multiple us-west-2 infer nodes; autoscaler responded but several pods dropped in the same 30s window.
- 08:40 PT: smart-router considered node availability and routed a portion of requests to us-east-1.
- 08:42–09:10 PT: error rate peaked at ~3.9%, p95 latency doubled for routed sessions.

Preliminary root causes being investigated: possible noisy tenant on a shared pool causing transient OOM/evictions + a suboptimal backoff window in the routing fallback logic.

Mitigation steps in progress:
- Isolated suspected noisy workloads; kicked them off the shared pool (manual cordon).
- Increased short-term capacity in us-west-2 (hotburst) and tightened routing fallback threshold to prefer slow local vs cross-region for pinned customers.
- Captured KV cache samples and prefix distributions (see Drive link).

I recommend we let Starlite continue on us-west-2 with the temporary hotburst and follow up with a post-mortem. If leadership wants to engage externally, let me know and I can prepare a short tech note.

-David
David Kim
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Evan —

Thanks for the quick report and for the logs. David is triaging now; we isolated a noisy tenant in the shared pool and triggered a short hotburst in us-west-2 which should reduce cross-region routing. You may continue to see elevated p95 for sessions that were routed, but new sessions should prefer the local region once the hotburst ramps.

What we'll do next:
- Short (2–4 hour) hotburst in us-west-2 to restore capacity and reflow traffic.
- After stabilization, we'll run a focused post-mortem and share findings and any recommended config changes to prevent noisy-tenant evictions.
- If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min sync for 11:30 PT to walk your infra team through the mitigations.

Marissa will track SLAs and credits if the incident crosses thresholds; I'll follow up with concrete timelines.

Apologies for the disruption — we know these cross-region switchover effects are painful.

— Monica
Monica Patel

Subject: Exec note: Starlite routing surge — quick summary for leadership

Looping in leadership context for transparency. Short brief for C-suite if asked:

- Impact: Production customers in us-west-2 experienced transient 5xx (peak ~4%) and p95 latency increase due to automated routing to us-east-1. A subset of routed sessions saw ~2x latency. Starlite reported user-visible customer tickets.
- Cause (prelim): Noisy tenant in a shared pool caused multiple node evictions; routing fallback logic favored cross-region fallbacks under current thresholds.
- Mitigation: Manual noisy-tenant isolation + hotburst capacity in us-west-2; reduced fallback aggressiveness.
- Status: Stabilized; error rate falling back toward baseline.
- Next steps: Full post-mortem (owner: David), routing policy change to prefer local degraded performance over cross-region fallback for pinned/priority customers (owner: Rishi), customer communication / SLA assessment (owner: Marissa).

If leadership wants to reach out to Starlite execs directly I can draft language; otherwise Marissa should own customer conversations re: credits.

-Markus

VP, Platform Engineering, Redwood Inference
